#724:## Summary
#724:
#724:Follow-up hardening of the unified FFmpeg admission gate. Three fixes land together because they touch the same primitive and the same producer call sites:
#724:
#724:- **Background audio prep no longer crowds out the next thing to air.** Prefetch renders (~75s on the Pi) and other background FFmpeg work now take a second bounded slot on top of the shared gate, so at least one of the two total slots always stays free for a next-to-air foreground render. [proof: tests]
#724:- **Emergency bridge audio gets a real priority path.** The rescue bypass is now wired at the genuine bridge/tone/silence construction sites, so recovery tones and silence fillers no longer queue behind routine processing; ordinary chimes and SFX stay bounded. [proof: tests]
#724:- **The admission primitive moved to its own home.** `_NORM_SEM` and `ffmpeg_slot` (with the new background and rescue parameters) now live in `mammamiradio/audio/admission.py`. Pure move, behavior unchanged. [proof: tests]
#724:
#724:A follow-up commit closes three review-found gaps on top of those fixes:
#724:
#724:- **Prefetch relaunch guard now has a regression test.** The loop-level decision to skip launching a second prefetch task while one is still in flight (the actual behavior change the "prefetch lane" fix makes) previously had zero integration-level coverage — every existing test exercised `_prefetch_next` in isolation. [proof: tests]
#724:- **The rescue-lane concurrency comment now describes real behavior.** It previously claimed a hard "1 rescue job" cap; the cap is best-effort, not hard — a wedged rescue render lets every subsequent rescue call proceed ungated too, for as long as the wedge lasts. This is intentional (a stuck rescue render must never delay the next dead-air fill), now documented accurately in `admission.py` and `docs/architecture.md` instead of silently wrong. [proof: tests]
#724:- **Two smaller coverage gaps closed**: the interrupt bridge tone's `rescue=True` kwarg is now asserted (previously unasserted, unlike its sibling tests), and the prewarm (instant-audio pre-roll) render call site now has a regression guard pinning it to the foreground admission lane. [proof: tests]
#724:
#724:A pre-existing, out-of-scope gap surfaced during review (`_prefetch_task` not tracked/cancelled at app shutdown) is filed separately as #726 rather than folded into this PR.
#724:
#724:A third commit addresses CodeRabbit's completed review: the session-pause path was still calling `_prefetch_task.cancel()`, which flips `done()` to `True` while the executor ffmpeg keeps running — so the relaunch guard could launch a *second* concurrent prefetch on resume, the exact race this PR closes elsewhere. That cancel call is now removed (left running, consistent with the "let it finish" fix above); the empty-fallback silence test now asserts its `rescue=True` kwarg instead of silently swallowing it; and the new prefetch regression test releases its blocked task before teardown instead of leaking it. [proof: tests]

#731:## Summary
#731:
#731:**New capability**
#731:- `mammamiradio/release_campaign.py` (new) — a durable state machine that turns an optional, packaged `release_beat.toml` manifest into a bounded, listener-safe on-air announcement after an update. Ships absent/disabled by default (complete no-op); when enabled, offers the scriptwriter a prompt block on the first eligible banter break, and only counts an airing once a segment actually reaches a connected listener.
#731:- `mammamiradio/restart_handoff.py` (new) — a small spool that copies a few already-normalized music tracks into `cache/restart_handoff/` as they play, so the next boot can admit them straight into the live queue before the producer warms up — a faster cold open after a restart than starting from an empty queue.
#731:- `scripts/validate-release-beat.py` (new) — validates the manifest's schema and listener-safe copy (blocks release-engineering words like "version" or "changelog" from reaching on-air lines unless explicitly allowlisted), wired into the release-invariants gate and the edge/stable release scripts.
#731:
#731:**Fixes from an internal review pass before this landed**
#731:- The campaign's never-aired throttle now keys on time only, not a segment counter that never resets for a beat that's never aired, and self-retires at the campaign window if the host keeps declining.
#731:- The restart-handoff spool prune can no longer delete a handoff file that's still queued for playback.
#731:- A missing or unreadable queued audio file is now skipped instead of crashing the playback loop.
#731:- A commit-free safety net restores a release-beat attempt that never reaches the queue, including when a sibling generation task fails.
#731:- The campaign ledger saves synchronously and stops writing to disk on every ordinary segment once a campaign has retired.
#731:- The manifest gate is wired into the edge and stable release scripts so a manifest that targets the wrong build/version blocks the release it doesn't match.
#731:
#731:**Documentation**
#731:- `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/operations.md`, `docs/runbooks/ha-addon.md`, `docs/REPO_MAP.md`, and the project instructions file updated to reflect the new startup step, the two new modules, the new `cache/` directory, and the release-invariants gate's new checks — no new routes, env vars, or config keys were introduced.
#731:

#735:## Summary
#735:
#735:Closes #729
#735:
#735:Startup now sweeps orphaned `.tmp` scratch files left behind by an interrupted restart-handoff spool write (a hard kill between `tempfile.mkstemp` and the final `os.replace` — the exact scenario an add-on update crash-kill produces). Without this, those files leaked disk space indefinitely across restarts, since neither existing cache-cleanup path scanned `cache/restart_handoff/` or its `segments/` subdirectory.
#735:
#735:**Core feature**
#735:- `prune_stale_handoff_tmp_files()` in `mammamiradio/restart_handoff.py`: prunes `.manifest-*.tmp` / `.handoff-*.tmp` files older than 6h from `cache/restart_handoff/` and `cache/restart_handoff/segments/`. Wired into `main.py`'s `startup()`, right after the existing `prune_stale_tmp_files` call.
#735:
#735:**Hardening (found via review, all fixed in this same PR)**
#735:- Fixed an uncaught-crash bug: `Path.resolve(strict=False)` raises `RuntimeError` (not `OSError`) on a symlink loop, and the new startup call had no surrounding try/except — unlike the analogous `_admit_restart_handoff` call, which is deliberately guarded for exactly this "never abort startup" reason. A corrupted/symlinked cache dir would have crashed the whole app at boot.
#735:- Added `max_age_hours` input validation (0/negative/NaN would otherwise compute a cutoff at-or-after "now" and prune everything, including a tmp file from a write in progress).
#735:- Added a per-directory cap (500 candidates, oldest-first) so a pathological backlog can't stall startup, plus a second, independent ceiling (5000 candidates) bounding the raw `glob()` enumeration itself — the first cap alone didn't stop `list(directory.glob(...))` and the oldest-first sort from costing unbounded scan time on an extreme backlog, a gap 4 independent review passes converged on (2 specialist subagents + Codex structured review + Codex adversarial exec).
#735:- Symlink and path-containment checks on both the scratch directories and individual candidate files, verified against real symlink loops and path-escape attempts (not mocked).
#735:- Runtime-behavior documentation updated to describe the new startup step, including both caps.
#735:
#735:**Deferred to its own PR** (tracked in #738, not bundled here per this repo's Scope Discipline rule): consolidating 4 independently-written path-containment-check implementations that now exist in `restart_handoff.py`, and unifying this new prune-loop with the structurally similar one in `playlist/downloader.py`.
#735:

#735:
#735:```

#735:├─ [x] symlink loop on cache_dir / handoff dir → RuntimeError caught, no-op

#737:## Summary
#737:
#737:- **Root cause found via HA Green log inspection.** Six of sixteen fictional ad brands in `radio.toml` had a jingle sound-effect signature naming a sound that doesn't exist (some were music-mood names like `cheap_synth_romance`, others invented names like `dust_hit` that were never implemented). Every one of those brands' jingles silently degraded to a plain default chime, every time, on every deployment — this is exactly what produced the "Unknown SFX type" warnings observed live on the addon. Corrected all six, synced the byte-for-byte HA addon copy, and added a guard test (`tests/core/test_config.py`) so an invalid `sonic_signature` fails CI instead of shipping silently.
#737:- **Separate, smaller issue in the ad-writing prompt.** The ad-generation LLM prompt listed the sound-effect vocabulary right next to the ad's music-bed/environment vocabulary without distinguishing them, so the model would sometimes reuse a music-bed name as a sound cue. The prompt now explicitly rules that out.
#737:- Added a regression test for the prompt change and a data-integrity test for the config fix.
#737:
#737:## QA Impact
#737:
#737:Classification: None
#737:Reason:
#737:- Touched surfaces: an ad-generation prompt string and a config data file (`radio.toml`) — no route, admin UI, listener UI, or API contract changed.
#737:- Why this QA scope is sufficient: the change is either LLM-prompt wording (unverifiable without a live model call, covered by a prompt-content regression test) or static config data with a new automated guard test. No user-facing surface changed.

#737:## Follow-up (not in scope for this PR)
#737:
#737:Adversarial review (Claude + Codex) both flagged that the ad-writing fix is prompt-compliance-only — there's no server-side validation clamping an LLM-emitted `sfx` value to `AVAILABLE_SFX_TYPES` in `write_ad`. The normalizer's existing fallback makes this safe (never dead air, just a generic chime), but a one-line clamp would close the bug class permanently instead of relying on the model following instructions. Flagging for a possible fast-follow; not fixing here to keep this PR scoped to the confirmed root cause.

#739:## Summary
#739:
#739:The Diretta pacing sliders (songs between host breaks, between ad breaks, ads per break) only mutated live config, so every add-on restart reset them to their defaults. They now persist, built on the existing persist-first / mutate-second toggle pattern (Super Italian, On-Air Sound, AI Quality) — no new architecture.
#739:
#739:### Key changes
#739:- `PATCH /api/pacing` persists every present key **before** mutating live config, under `_pacing_lock`. The add-on write is ONE atomic `_save_addon_option_batch` into `/data/options.json` (a partial write of three separate keys could half-update it); standalone writes `.env`. A failed write returns 500 and leaves both live and durable config untouched, so they cannot disagree after a restart. [proof: tests]
#739:- `_save_dotenv` now holds `_DOTENV_LOCK`, so two concurrent admin saves of different settings can no longer lose each other's `.env` update (a pre-existing race across the four toggles, closed at the primitive). [proof: tests]
#739:- `core/config.py` reads `MAMMAMIRADIO_PACING_*` at boot (env > `radio.toml`), each clamped to the `_validate` bounds so a stale or hand-edited value degrades to the clamp instead of failing boot. `_apply_addon_options` maps the three keys for the non-`run.sh` add-on path.
#739:- The add-on exposes **Songs between host breaks / Songs between ad breaks / Ads per break** (stable + edge `config.yaml`, `run.sh`, `en.yaml`); defaults match `radio.toml` (2 / 4 / 2).
#739:- Each change records an `operator_action` ledger row.
#739:
#739:### Docs
#739:- The three `MAMMAMIRADIO_PACING_*` env vars, their precedence and clamp bounds, and the persist-first/atomic contract are documented alongside the other add-on settings.
#739:- `CHANGELOG.md` + `ha-addon/mammamiradio/CHANGELOG.md`: human-readable "your pacing settings now stick" entry.
#739:
#739:No version bump — the repo is already at 2.15.0 (versions are set at release time, not per PR).

#741:Closes #688
#741:
#741:## What
#741:
#741:The five provider credential fields (`anthropic_api_key`, `openai_api_key`, `azure_speech_key`, `azure_speech_region`, `elevenlabs_api_key`) are removed from the HA add-on options schema — stable and edge `config.yaml` plus both `translations/en.yaml`. This finishes the secrets migration started in #699: keys live only in `/config/secrets.env`, so a fresh install never exposes them to `ha addons info` [proof: tests].
#741:
#741:## Why
#741:
#741:Supervisor add-on options are printed by routine diagnostics and support snippets. #699 moved reads/writes to `secrets.env` but kept the schema fields as a compatibility window; that window has passed and the fields are now the only remaining place a provider key could land in Supervisor options.
#741:
#741:## Rebased onto #742 + #739 — real conflict, not just adjacent lines
#741:
#741:#742 ("declutter configuration options") and #739 (pacing sliders) merged into `main` while this branch was open, both touching the same `config.yaml` region. #742 kept the 5 provider fields *in* `schema:` and only hid them from the visible `options:` defaults (HA's "show unused optional configuration options" disclosure) — a UX declutter, not a security fix, since a schema-only field is still a real, settable Supervisor option that Supervisor persists and `ha addons info` still prints once set. #742 never references or closes #688.
#741:
#741:This branch is rebased onto the merged result: kept #742's Configuration-tab reordering and #739's new pacing fields, and additionally removed the 5 provider fields from `schema:` entirely — the only change that actually stops them from reaching Supervisor's persisted options. `jamendo_client_id` stays schema-only-hidden per #742's design (out of #688's scope, not a provider secret). One of #742's own regression tests asserted the 5 fields stay schema-present; updated to assert `jamendo_client_id` alone stays hidden-but-present while the 5 provider fields are absent from both `options:` and `schema:` entirely.
#741:
#741:## Upgrade path (the part that needed real design)
#741:
#741:Supervisor validates stored options against the new schema when it starts the add-on and drops unknown keys from `/data/options.json` — so the existing `run.sh` options.json fallback alone would have silently stripped every upgraded install's keys on first boot (hosts degrade to stock copy with no error). `run.sh` therefore gains a one-time, best-effort recovery: when a provider key is missing from both `secrets.env` and `options.json`, it fetches the values still held in Supervisor's stored settings (`GET /addons/self/info`, token-authenticated, 5s timeout) and persists them into `secrets.env` (0600, atomic write), so every later boot is file-first. Any failure warns and boots without those keys — never a boot failure [proof: tests].
#741:
#741:Honest residual: previously saved values remain visible in Supervisor's stored settings until the operator opens the Configuration tab and saves once; docs now say so instead of overpromising.
#741:
#741:## Guards
#741:
#741:- `test_addon_schema_has_no_provider_secret_fields`: regex-based check that no provider field reappears in either channel's `options:`/`schema:`/translations, plus the inverse pin that `run.sh` keeps its legacy fallback map [proof: tests].
#741:- 4 new run.sh parser tests: recovery round-trip against a stub Supervisor endpoint (persist + 0600 + second-boot file-first), `secrets.env` precedence over the store, no-token skip, unreachable-API fail-soft [proof: tests].
#741:- `tests/workflows/test_validate_addon_edge.sh` schema-drift probe retargeted to a surviving field (it mutated a now-removed key, which turned the CI self-test into a silent no-op) [proof: addon].
#741:- `test_addon_manifest_hides_legacy_optional_fields_but_keeps_admin_token_visible` (from #742) updated to match the post-rebase schema shape rather than asserting the now-removed provider fields stay present [proof: tests].
#741:
#741:## Pre-Landing Review
#741:
#741:Three parallel reviewers plus a cross-model pass ran on the diff before the rebase; all blocking findings were fixed:
#741:- CI self-test no-op in the edge-block scenarios (fixed, see Guards).
#741:- Supervisor strips schema-removed keys from `options.json` at first start, defeating the planned fallback (fixed via the boot recovery above).
#741:- Docs overpromised that `ha addons info` stops printing keys for upgraded installs (reworded to fresh-install scope + clear-on-save tip).
#741:- Guard test was substring-based and blind to quoted/spaced YAML keys (hardened to a regex).

#743:
#743:## Why only uv.lock
#743:
#743:`requirements.txt` (pip-compile output) already carries these exact patched versions from an earlier regeneration — but nothing in CI or the Dockerfile installs from it (`pip install -e .` reads `pyproject.toml` directly). `uv.lock` is the one manifest that actually backs local `uv sync` dev installs, and it was the one still pinned to the vulnerable versions — hence the alerts.
#743:
#743:No other dependency moved; ran with `uv lock --upgrade-package <name>` per package, not a general `uv lock --upgrade`.

#744:## Decision Record
#744:
#744:- Ship the LLM mood scene namer disabled by default. The existing mood ladder remains the synchronous behavior and fallback, so normal station operation keeps the same latency and reliability profile.
#744:- Use a background refresh plus TTL cache instead of blocking BANTER, AD, or NEWS_FLASH production on model latency.
#744:- Track Home mood spend under its own `script_home_mood` category so operators can see whether the experiment is worth turning on.
#744:- Prefer the scored HA context over new entity-specific ladder rules because the scored set is the integration boundary already meant to generalize across homes.
#744:- Serve the scene stale-while-revalidate (15-minute staleness cap) instead of dying exactly at the TTL: mood consumers are minutes apart at default pacing, so a TTL-exact cache would be paid for on every segment yet almost never heard. The TTL stays the refresh/attempt spacing, so cost is unchanged.
#744:- Keep the LLM scene on the public Casa card: scene validation enforces a structural allowlist (letters-only, 1-6 words after Unicode normalization) and rejects resident names from person entities, so the public surface stays within the same bounds as the aired banter.
#744:- Defer fencing the mood inside the banter prompt's read-only data block: the value is opt-in, off by default, and allowlist-bounded, while re-fencing would change prompt semantics for the heuristic ladder moods too. Revisit if the experiment earns default-on.
#744:

#745:## Summary
#745:
#745:Ships **direction-based song selection**: operators steer the next music stretch from free text ("2000s female vocals", "sunday morning italian"). Typed text expands into concrete song targets (LLM with a curated fallback), yt-dlp resolves them, matches download in the background, and a per-course budget biases upcoming picks toward the tagged tracks. The course persists across restarts and never interrupts what's playing.
#745:
#745:Bundles the feature plus a hardening pass that closed verified async races and made the operator feedback truthful under failure:
#745:
#745:- Persisted-course writes serialize under `source_switch_lock` with a fresh identity re-check, so a write racing "Back to auto" can't resurrect a just-cleared course on the next restart. [proof: tests]
#745:- Direction downloads register for shutdown cancellation at creation — a cancelled request can't leak them past teardown. [proof: tests]
#745:- A duplicate submit while downloads are still in flight is a no-op on the same course, not a second competing course. [proof: tests]
#745:- The wait for the first track to land is time-bounded: on timeout the course stays live and downloads keep going (audio never blocks), and the admin banner/toast say "finding songs…" instead of claiming it is already steering. Only a genuine all-downloads-failed rolls back to automatic rotation. [proof: tests]
#745:- Direction searches use a dedicated thread pool so they can't starve the admin song search; the post-restart restore resolves targets concurrently and bounded. Failed, dropped, or banned downloads surface an operator notice instead of vanishing. [proof: tests]
#745:
#745:Behaviour is documented in `docs/architecture.md` (cache/heading.json) and `CHANGELOG.md`.

#748:## Summary
#748:
#748:Live incident on the HA Green edge add-on: host banter kept degrading to generic stock filler. Root cause chain: the banter writer's response was cut off at its token budget (the demanded output — warranted 4-6 exchanges plus persona memory fields — outgrew 1200 tokens), and the backup writer then returned an empty completion at the same starved budget. Every failure aired pre-written filler instead of real banter. [proof: tests]
#748:
#748:- Banter budget raised 1200 → 2400 (`_BANTER_MAX_TOKENS`, floor-guarded by a test; same class of budget was outgrown once before at 600 → 1200).
#748:- One escalated retry (×1.75) when a response is cut at its budget, decided before the no-backup-key check so single-provider installs retry too; the serialization lock is acquired per attempt so short scripts interleave between a long retry's attempts.
#748:- Per-attempt wall-clock scales with the requested budget (45-120s) under a 180s ceiling that never gates the base fallback ladder; the backup call is also capped by the remaining ceiling with a 45s floor.
#748:- After budget-exhausted failures the backup writer inherits the escalated budget as its floor; an empty or budget-cut backup completion gets one escalated retry of its own — unless the model reports it finished or refused, which a bigger budget cannot fix.
#748:- The backup client sends an HTTP-level timeout and no SDK-internal retries, so an abandoned request can no longer keep billing unrecorded calls.
#748:- Attempt telemetry stays honest: retried attempts are labelled as retrying (not as a provider fallback that never happened) and carry their real token spend; a WARNING fires when a successful generation uses ≥80%% of its budget, so the next contract growth announces itself before it truncates on air. [proof: tests]
#748:
#748:Pre-written filler remains the terminal fallback on every path — the stream never goes silent. [proof: tests]
#748:

#748:- Why this QA scope is sufficient: no listener or admin route, template, asset, or control changes; playback, queueing, and audio pipelines untouched. Automated checks cover the changed behavior (13 targeted tests on the retry mechanism).

#750:Makes the two station language modes do what their names promise. **Super Italian Mode on → hosts speak 100% Italian** (the old "English is rare and intentional" escape hatch is gone; only song/artist/brand names and the Bavarian guest's phraselets are exempt). **Off (default) → hosts speak roughly 70% English / 30% Italian** — English carries the information, Italian carries greetings, exclamations, punchlines, and about one line in three may be a whole Italian sentence, replacing the old "sprinkles, never full sentences."
#750:
#750:The fix is one centralized language policy in `hosts/prompt_world.py` (`language_mode_directive` + `language_mode_rule`) injected at every LLM speech surface — banter, course-change notices, news flashes, the weather-report override, ads, and transitions. Previously only banter followed the mode while news/ads/transitions hardcoded all-Italian, so normal mode aired full-Italian news inside an English-led show; now the whole station speaks one language policy per mode. [proof: tests]

#770:## Summary
#770:
#770:- `/public-status` used to fabricate its `upcoming` schedule (`predicted_from_playlist`) from the playlist rotation whenever the render queue was empty — showing listeners and third-party integrators songs that weren't actually cued to play. `upcoming` now only ever lists real, render-ready `rendered_queue` segments; an empty queue reports `upcoming_mode: "building"` instead.
#770:- The listener page and admin producer desk no longer pad four fake "Building schedule…" placeholder rows. Each now shows one honest status line distinguishing three states: station paused, no music source configured (`golden_path.stage === 'needs_music_source'`), and still building.
#770:- Docs updated in the same commit: `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/integrations/README.md`, `docs/integrations/migration-from-public-status.md` (adds an empty-queue decision table for integrators), `docs/integrations/now-playing.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
#770:- Two integration tests added closing gaps found in review: a combined no-music-source + empty-queue response, and a combined session-stopped + no-music-source response, so the backend contract can't silently decouple those signals again.
#770:- Tightened the Italian "no source" copy for register.
#770:

#770:- Why this QA scope is sufficient: both listener and admin UI branch logic changed for the empty-queue states; the public API response shape changed for third-party integrators.

#775:## Summary
#775:
#775:When the producer cannot build the intended segment and no recorded recovery clip is available, it now tries a short branded recovery sweeper before falling back to generated silence. The sweeper build is time-bounded, and rescue fills skip transition-sting work so the final safety net still wins if speech or imaging is slow.

#775:This also updates the recovery contract in the operator docs and both public changelogs.

#777:## Summary
#777:
#777:This PR implements the HA Green performance strategy's first two low-risk scopes without touching the running HA Green add-on.
#777:
#777:**Home Assistant context load**
#777:- Splits full Home Assistant prompt-context ingestion from HA entity publishing with `ha_context_enabled` / `MAMMAMIRADIO_HA_CONTEXT_ENABLED`.
#777:- Raises the default full `/api/states` prompt-context poll interval to 300 seconds and exposes `ha_context_poll_interval` / `MAMMAMIRADIO_HA_CONTEXT_POLL_INTERVAL`.
#777:- Keeps stale/empty context fallback and the existing `context_refresh_timeout` behavior.
#777:
#777:**Home Assistant add-on contract**
#777:- Mirrors the new options in stable and edge add-on manifests, translations, `run.sh`, root `radio.toml`, and add-on `radio.toml`.
#777:- Documents how operators can keep HA entities/timer interrupts while disabling prompt-context polling.
#777:
#777:**HACS and REST churn**
#777:- Makes the HACS coordinator send `If-None-Match` and reuse the prior `RadioStatus` on `304 Not Modified`.
#777:- Dedupes unchanged REST-pushed auxiliary sensor/binary payloads while preserving media-player heartbeat and bounded recovery republish for HA restarts.
#777:
#777:**Scope intentionally not included**
#777:- No version bump or changelog entry: this is not a release PR.
#777:- No bounded download/ad fan-out lane yet: the plan gates that on evidence that CPU spikes remain after the lower-risk HA polling/churn work ships.
#777:- No live HA Green operations were performed.
#777:
#777:## Test Coverage
#777:
#777:All new code paths have focused automated coverage:
#777:- config/env parsing, including invalid and non-positive poll intervals: `tests/core/test_config.py`, `tests/core/test_config_env_overrides.py`
#777:- add-on parser/schema parity: `tests/repo/test_run_sh_options_parser.py`
#777:- producer `context_enabled` gate: `tests/scheduling/test_producer_extended.py`
#777:- HA REST push dedupe/recovery: `tests/home/test_ha_context.py`, `tests/home/test_ha_media_player_push_flag.py`
#777:- HACS ETag/304 reuse: `tests_integration/test_coordinator.py`

#785:Cut the edge (dev) channel to `e68fd76`. The edge add-on's `version:` is the image tag
#785:the Supervisor pulls (`ghcr.io/florianhorner/mammamiradio-addon-{arch}:e68fd76`), so the soak Pi
#785:shows an in-place Update.
#785:
#785:`e68fd76` is the newest `main` commit with a green `Build HA Addon` image (that run is the
#785:proof both per-arch images were pushed). It may trail `origin/main` HEAD (e68fd76) when
#785:the tip commits touch only files that do not rebuild the image (tests/docs/CI); no `:<sha>`
#785:image exists for those, so pinning to the newest *built* commit is what guarantees the Update
#785:can actually pull. Manual edge release; stable is untouched.

#787:## Summary
#787:
#787:- Add `scripts/pr-queue-status.sh`: a read-only advisory dashboard for multi-PR landing sessions. For each open PR it reports merge state, the mapped local Conductor worktree, dirty/clean status, and a `land now` / `update + test` / `commit dirty work` / `conflict/manual` / `wait/checks` recommendation. `scripts/land-pr.sh` remains the only required landing path; this script never fetches, merges, comments, or edits PRs, branches, or worktrees.
#787:- Document the convention in `docs/agents.md` (PR Landing Queue section) and point to the new script from `scripts/land-pr.sh`'s header as an optional preflight.
#787:- Pre-ship review squad (testing, maintainability, performance, security specialists) found and I fixed: a real local-scoping bug shellcheck caught mid-refactor (a `local` statement using a variable before it took effect in the same statement), redundant `git worktree list` re-enumeration per PR (now cached once), and control flow coupled to a free-text display string (now an explicit clean/dirty status token). Security review found nothing.
#787:- Added test coverage for the worktree-matching fallback used by real Conductor workspaces (locally-renamed branch tracking a differently-named PR head via upstream), the `gh pr list` failure and malformed-JSON die paths, the `local origin/main unavailable` branch, and draft/conflict/checks-pending recommendation branches.

#793:## Summary
#793:
#793:- Stops Resume and idle wake-up from replaying the same packaged continuity clip when cached music can provide runway: the playback ladder serves the clip once per empty-queue gap, escalates to the norm cache and bundled demo music, and repeats the clip only when no eligible music exists anywhere.
#793:- Shares packaged-asset cleanup protection between producer and stream paths so bundled recovery audio is not treated as temp output.
#793:- Probes rescue-fill durations through the bounded rescue ffmpeg slot (playback ladder, resume/idle bridges, error recovery) and caches each packaged clip's duration, so a dead-air fill can never queue behind busy normalization jobs [proof: runtime].
#793:- Keys the /healthz and /readyz silence gate on nothing airing at all instead of queue emptiness, so a fresh install audibly bridging on the continuity clip during its first track render no longer reports failing or invites a watchdog restart [proof: tests].
#793:- Hardens the local merge guard against raw REST and GraphQL API merge attempts while keeping repo read-only API checks allowed.
#793:- Regression tests pin the ladder invariants: one clip per gap with the silence clock still running, second timeout reaching the norm cache, last-resort clip repeat on empty caches, no forced-banter double-fire past 60s, and the clip re-arming for the next gap after real audio [proof: tests]. Committed runtime evidence exercises the real loop with real files and real timing across warm-cache, empty-cache, and saturated-ffmpeg scenarios [proof: runtime].
#793:

#793:- Why this QA scope is sufficient: the changed behavior is exercised end-to-end by committed unmocked playback-loop runs (clip -> cached-song sequencing, empty-cache repeats, saturated-ffmpeg first-byte timing) plus the full test suite; there is nothing player- or admin-visible to click through beyond what those runs already prove.

#795:## Summary
#795:
#795:The station already reacts on air when something happens in the home — the coffee machine waking up, the fridge raided again, a leak sensor crying for help — but the reaction evaporated the moment it played. A listener couldn't tell a home-triggered line from generic banter, and an operator couldn't answer "why did the host just say that?" or "why did nothing happen?".
#795:
#795:**Moment Receipts** records every ritual-recipe moment from match through confirmed air and surfaces it on both pages:
#795:
#795:- **Listener page:** a "Live from your home" strip on the Casa card shows the last few aired home moments as plain labels ("Morning launch · 2 min ago"). Only generic family labels and a coarse age reach the unauthenticated surface — no device names, entity ids, confidence values, or spoken lines [proof: tests]
#795:- **Admin panel:** a "Home moments" trail (last 25) shows each moment's full story in plain words — made it to air, on air right now, cut short by a skip, played to an empty room, held back by a cooldown, stepped aside for another moment, bumped by a live cut-in, set aside by a mute, or cut off by a restart. Status codes never reach the screen.
#795:- **Honest by construction:** a moment only counts as "made it to air" once it truly streamed to a listener; backup clips and rescue audio never claim credit for the house, and every path where a carried moment dies before air demotes its row with a reason [proof: tests]
#795:- **New module** `mammamiradio/home/moment_receipts.py` (`MomentStore`): bounded store at `cache_dir/moments.json` (100 rows, 7-day retention, atomic writes, corrupt-tolerant load, cache-protected). Disk writes happen only from the producer loop; the playback loop mutates in memory and never does JSON I/O [proof: tests]
#795:- The moment id travels through the scriptwriter's consume/restore handoff into the carrying segment's metadata as an opaque token, so a fresh home event mid-generation can never attach the wrong receipt, and nothing about the home rides segment metadata onto public payloads [proof: tests]
#795:- The evening-gag ledger gains `ritual_family` provenance (`HomeEvent → GagBucket`), which also upgrades a bucket's label to the generic family label so a device name can never become a receipt label [proof: tests]
#795:- Docs updated in the same change: changelog headline entry, `docs/architecture.md` "Moment Receipts" section + route-table rows, and the agent-facing runtime notes.
#795:- Follow-up filed: #794 (`ambient_context` delivery lane is dead code — 2 of 12 families never air; the new panel will make that visible).
#795:
#795:No version bump — versioning stays a deliberate release action.
#795:

#797:## Summary
#797:
#797:- Fixed `generate_transition_sting()` in `mammamiradio/audio/normalizer.py`: `time_check` and `sweeper` were missing from its `speech_types` set, so every `music<->time_check` and `music<->sweeper` boundary fell through to a bare, unlayered synthesized sweep tone instead of the layered motif+bumper sting every other segment type (`banter`, `news_flash`, `ad`, `station_id`) gets. Producer-level code already treated both as speech-boundary types (`_SPEECH_TYPES` in `scheduling/producer.py`) — this was a local, string-literal duplicate of that enumeration that had silently drifted.
#797:- Bumped `SYNTH_CACHE_VERSION` (`1` -> `2`) in `mammamiradio/audio/synth_cache.py` so already-cached bare-sweep stings on a running instance are invalidated and regenerated with the fix, instead of continuing to serve the stale audio from cache (`synth_*.mp3` files are exempt from every startup purge).
#797:- Added a contract test that derives `speech_types` coverage from the `SegmentType` enum itself, so a future segment type addition fails loudly instead of silently repeating this bug a third time.
#797:- CHANGELOG entries (root + HA add-on) describing the listener-facing fix.
#797:
#797:## Test Coverage
#797:
#797:Tests: 23 -> 26 in `tests/audio/test_normalizer_imaging.py` (+3: `music->time_check`, `time_check->music`, plus one contract test covering every non-music `SegmentType`; the `sweeper` pair is covered by two dedicated tests plus the contract test). Full suite: 4371 passed, 2 skipped.
#797:
#797:Every code path the diff touches (`generate_transition_sting`, its caller `pick_stinger`) was traced end to end; no coverage gap found.
#797:
#797:## Pre-Landing Review
#797:
#797:No issues found. This diff is exactly the "Enum & Value Completeness" checklist category (adding a value to a hardcoded set) — checked for sibling definitions of the same set elsewhere in the codebase; `speech_types` is defined in exactly one place.
#797:
#797:## Adversarial Review
#797:
#797:Two independent review passes surfaced a sibling gap and a cache-staleness risk before this shipped: the `sweeper` segment type had the identical missing-set bug as `time_check` (same function, one enum value away), and bumping the code without also bumping the cache version would have left already-running instances silently serving the old bare-sweep audio from cache. Both were verified by reading the code directly and fixed in this same PR. Final pass: clean, no outstanding findings.
#797:

#807:## Adversarial Review
#807:
#807:Claude subagent + Codex adversarial + Codex structured review, run in parallel, then a verification re-run after fixes:
#807:- **[P1, cross-model confirmed by both Codex passes]** Reduced-motion dedica submitters saw an invisible (opacity:0) confirmation — fixed.
#807:- **[Claude adversarial]** No fetch timeout on the dedica submit guard — a stalled connection could permanently disable the submit button with no error shown. Fixed with an 8s `AbortController` timeout; a Codex re-review then caught that the timeout was cleared before the response body finished reading (not just headers) — fixed that too.
#807:- **[Claude adversarial]** `aria-live` confirmation text was set while hidden, then only revealed via a later style change — screen readers may not announce it. Fixed by re-asserting the text mutation at reveal time.
#807:- **[Codex adversarial]** `tt-wake`'s `animation-fill-mode: both` permanently overwrote `.mmr-nav`'s static `transform: translateZ(0)` compositor-layer hint (added to avoid sticky+backdrop-filter scroll flicker) with `translateY(0)`. Fixed — nav now gets a fade-only entrance variant.
#807:- **[Codex adversarial]** Admin typewriter could leave the diagnostic panel visibly incomplete for many seconds on an unusually long line. Fixed with a 200-char cap that falls back to instant render.
#807:- **[Claude adversarial, INVESTIGATE]** A pre-existing mobile breakpoint removes title-overflow clipping; combined with the new roll animation's "from" state, the incoming title could briefly bleed below the meta block on narrow viewports. Defensively re-clipped only during the animation.
#807:- **[Claude adversarial, INVESTIGATE, accepted]** The page-entrance fade runs on every load regardless of connection speed — a deliberate Act I tradeoff (already reasoned through: gating on data-readiness would risk a worse blank-page regression on slow cold boots). Worth a follow-up Lighthouse/LCP check, not blocking.

#808:## What this does
#808:
#808:Moves all AI model identity out of `radio.toml` into a canonical sibling file,
#808:`model_registry.toml`: model IDs, task-to-role routing, quality profiles, the
#808:OpenAI TTS model, and per-model token pricing. Swapping a model is now a
#808:configuration-only release.
#808:
#808:The PR also makes the existing AI Quality dial a real three-tier contract:
#808:
#808:- `premium`: Opus for Anthropic creative work and the large OpenAI creative fallback
#808:- `balanced` (default): Sonnet and the small OpenAI creative fallback
#808:- `economy`: Haiku and the small OpenAI creative fallback
#808:- latency-sensitive fast work: Haiku/small in every profile
#808:
#808:`GET` and `POST /api/quality` keep the same profile names and payloads. A live
#808:switch never interrupts or purges the current segment; it changes only future
#808:generated work.
#808:
#808:`resolve_model()` returns `Optional[str]`: when the registry is missing or
#808:malformed, routes resolve to `None` and every caller degrades to stock host copy
#808:or Edge TTS rather than sending `model=None` to a provider. The station still
#808:boots and plays music [proof: tests].
#808:
#808:## How it ships safely
#808:
#808:- The registry is bundled into the standalone Docker image and HA add-on. CI and
#808:  `validate-addon.sh` hash-assert the installed copy against the canonical root
#808:  file, so a build that drops the registry fails [proof: build].
#808:- `load_config` resolves the registry beside `radio.toml`, matching the station's
#808:  existing configuration layout.
#808:- A legacy `[models]` block in an older `radio.toml` remains read-only compatible
#808:  with a deprecation warning; it is never a new canonical source.
#808:
#808:## QA Impact
#808:
#808:Classification: operator-visible configuration behavior change.
#808:
#808:- Listener audio delivery, admin API names, authentication, and queue semantics
#808:  are unchanged.
#808:- An operator selecting a profile now receives the documented creative quality and
#808:  cost tier on the next generated segment. Fast transitions remain on the
#808:  low-latency route in every tier.
#808:- Coverage asserts the full shipped profile matrix, every creative and fast caller,
#808:  the live Balanced-to-Premium API switch, OpenAI fallback selection, and provider
#808:  health-check deduplication [proof: tests].
#808:- The add-on schema and mappings are unchanged; its canonical-registry preflight
#808:  passes locally. CI verifies the installed image hash [proof: build].

#809:## Summary
#809:
#809:- Consolidate restart-handoff and downloader containment checks through one fail-closed path helper (`mammamiradio/core/path_safety.py`).
#809:- Reject symlinked cache candidates and validate handoff and segments destinations before a spool write creates files.
#809:- Keep stale temporary-file cleanup within the same containment contract, with regression coverage for symlink escapes and resolution failures.
#809:- **Two adversarial review passes (Codex + Claude subagent, run independently) found the same class of bug from different angles and both are now fixed:** `safe_path_within(path, root, reject_symlinks=True)` only ever rejected a symlinked *leaf*, never a symlinked *root* — root and path both resolve through the same redirect, so containment held trivially even though both pointed outside the intended directory.
#809:  - `restart_handoff.py`: a symlinked `cache/restart_handoff` let startup admission read a manifest and enqueue audio from outside the cache — the sha256 check offered no protection since the same redirected location also controls the manifest recording the hash. Fixed by routing `_resolve_relative_to_handoff` and `load_restart_handoff_manifest` through `_safe_handoff_dir`, which independently validates the handoff root against the resolved cache dir first.
#809:  - `downloader.py`: `prune_stale_tmp_files` used `tmp_dir` as both the glob root and the containment root. Unlike a symlinked leaf (`unlink()` never dereferences), a symlinked `tmp_dir` root meant every glob/stat/unlink targeted real files in the redirected directory — empirically confirmed real file deletion outside `tmp_dir`. Fixed with an explicit `tmp_dir.is_symlink()` guard.
#809:  - Both were empirically verified with a PoC before and after the fix (see commit `1b6d30bc`).
#809:- Removed now-dead code in `_prune_stale_tmp_glob` (the `directory.is_symlink()` branches became unreachable once `reject_symlinks=True` rejects a symlinked root earlier in the same function) — flagged independently by CodeRabbit and this review's maintainability specialist.

#811:## Summary
#811:
#811:- **Host banter no longer implies an already-played song is coming up.** A line referencing a track that already aired could read as forward-looking ("and after that... Baby Bird") even though the schedule itself was correct. The shared host system prompt now bans forward-sounding connectors ("next", "coming up", "after that") when referencing an already-played track and requires clearly-past framing instead.
#811:- **A related latent race is closed.** `write_transition()`'s "just finished playing" claim is spoken directly over the crossfaded audio tail of the previous song — but the underlying `played_tracks` history is recorded at production/enqueue time, not confirmed on-air time. An operator air-next front-insert landing between when a transition is scripted and when it airs could make that claim genuinely false. `_front_insert_queue_and_shadow` now detects and drops a stale-claim queue head before front-inserting, mirroring the existing audio-level guard for a related bug (#641).
#811:- **Pre-ship review caught and fixed two more issues**: the new internal tracking key (`transition_track_ref`) was leaking a track's cache key into the public `/public-status` API — added to the existing internal-metadata denylist with a regression test; and the metadata-threading through the real `run_producer()` pipeline had no integration-level test — added one for both the banter and ad-break paths.
#811:
#811:Root cause traced via HA Green's `docker logs` + provenance ledger (read-only production inspection, no live changes) against the actual playback timeline.

#812:## What
#812:
#812:The admin "Find records" (Record Hunt) box lets an operator steer the station toward a mood or era. It tagged matching tracks with a fixed selection weight of 4x. Against a rotation pool of up to 200 songs, an ~8-track hunt won only about 1 pick in 6, so operators heard their steering only occasionally and read it as ignored. The steering worked; the nudge was too weak to perceive. [proof: runtime]
#812:
#812:## Change
#812:
#812:Replace the fixed 4x bump with a pool-size-aware lift that targets ~45% of picks regardless of pool size, clamped to `[4.0, 60.0]`:
#812:
#812:- Small pools keep the old 4x floor, so existing behavior is unchanged there.
#812:- A tiny hunt set can never make one song dominate the station (60x cap).
#812:- Cooldowns, bans, artist diversity, and pinned tracks still win as hard overrides. Selection stays steering, not queue control.
#812:
#812:Implemented as a two-pass weight computation in `select_next_track` (base weights plus split sums, then one adaptive multiplier). Verified by six new unit tests across every branch of the lift and a 6000-pick simulation showing the delivered hunt share rise from 17.6% (old 4x) to 44.2% (adaptive). [proof: runtime]
#812:

#812:
#812:Classification: Player / Deferred to release candidate
#812:
#812:Reason:
#812:- Touched surfaces: song selection weighting (which songs air). No UI, route, config, env, or auth change.
#812:- Why this QA scope is sufficient: the effect is a share-over-many-songs shift that manual clicking cannot observe in a short session. It is covered by deterministic unit tests across every branch of the lift plus a 6000-pick simulation. Full Player and Admin QA run on the release candidate.

#813:## Summary
#813:
#813:Fixes the admin "Scaletta" (Live Queue / rundown) panel reading "0 ready" while real audio was already playing.
#813:
#813:- **Root cause fix (`mammamiradio/scheduling/producer.py`, `mammamiradio/main.py`):** startup prewarms, continuity bridges, and the two silence-quality-gate rescue paths queued real audio through `_enqueue_with_egress()` without a matching admin shadow row. Worse, `streamer.py`'s `queued_segments.pop(0)` on consumption assumes a strict 1:1 row-per-segment invariant, so consuming an unshadowed segment popped an *unrelated* row and desynced the whole shadow list from the real queue. A shared `_queue_shadow_entry(segment, *, reason=None)` helper now stamps `queue_id` and builds the shadow row in one place; `_enqueue_with_egress` auto-builds it whenever a caller omits one, and `main.py`'s restart-handoff admission reuses the same helper instead of hand-rolling an identical dict.
#813:- **Admin UI (`mammamiradio/web/templates/admin.html`):** the Scaletta toolbar now reads "The hosts are N minutes/seconds ahead" instead of a raw buffered-seconds counter, with sub-minute precision preserved (a 2-second buffer reads "2 seconds ahead", not a falsely-reassuring "1 minute ahead") and per-filter counts restored when a Music/Banter/Ads pill is active ("1 of 12 cued."). The `aria-live="polite"` runway region only mutates the DOM when the announced text actually changes, so it doesn't re-announce identical text to screen readers on every ~2s poll.
#813:- **Docs:** `docs/architecture.md`'s admission matrix and both `CHANGELOG.md` files updated in the same commits.

#816:## Summary
#816:
#816:Adds a floor-first correctness gate for host-segment script output.
#816:
#816:**New module** `mammamiradio/hosts/segment_floor.py` — a pure, I/O-free `check_floor(segment, raw_output, config)` that turns parsed LLM output into a tri-state PASS/FAIL/N/A receipt across three gates built from existing guards: station-name (foreign prefix-form names), banter-roster (a named host must be in the roster), and spoken-text (a spoken segment must carry airable text). `direction` and `memory_extract` are intentionally N/A (playlist targets / post-air control plane, not spoken copy). No audio-path wiring — this is the single source of truth the eval uses now and any future runtime gate can import.
#816:
#816:**Eval wiring** `scripts/eval_openai_script_model.py` — the paid OpenAI-fallback evaluator now records a per-gate receipt in schema-versioned JSONL, keeping raw-output integrity failures separate from provider/JSON failures. Adds a no-network `--dry-run` preflight (fixture validation plus paid-call and cost bounds), an `--allow-unpriced` gate, microsecond run ids, and creates the output dir before the paid run so a bad `--output-dir` can no longer burn a run and lose every receipt [proof: runtime].
#816:
#816:Fixture hosts updated Sofia to Giulia to match the configured roster.
#816:

#821:## Summary

#821:**Fix**
#821:- The mid-playback drain recovery bridge (`_queue_drain_recovery_bridge` in `mammamiradio/scheduling/producer.py`) now passes `music_runway=True` to the shared `_queue_continuity_bridge` helper, matching the Resume and idle-wakeup bridges. When active playback drains (queue hits zero mid-session, not just on Resume/idle-wakeup), the station now queues one cached music track right behind the branded continuity clip instead of looping the same short host line while the producer catches up.

#821:
#821:**Fixed during review:** the performance specialist flagged that the new drain code path increases how often `_queue_norm_cache_bridge_segment` calls `select_norm_cache_rescue` synchronously inside an `async def` (blocking `glob()` + per-file sidecar reads on the event loop). Wrapped it in `asyncio.to_thread` to match the existing pattern used two lines above in the same function — **then reverted** after Codex adversarial review caught that the naive thread-offload reads live mutable `StationState` (a `deque` mutated on the event loop) from a worker thread, risking an uncaught `RuntimeError: deque mutated during iteration` that would permanently kill the fire-and-forget producer task. Filed as a properly-scoped follow-up instead of a quick fix under time pressure — see below.

#822:## Home Context Director
#822:
#822:Casual host breaks used to read like a dashboard: the same home details could surface twice within a lookahead window, and room-presence sensors were fair game with no consent. This adds a session-scoped director that gives each casual break at most one allowlisted ambient Home Assistant cue, holds that topic out for 30 minutes after it actually airs, and keeps room-presence off until an operator explicitly opts a sensor in.
#822:
#822:### What changed
#822:- **New `mammamiradio/home/context_director.py`** — pure selection + reservation/cooldown engine. It owns only selection and queue-lifecycle bookkeeping: it never polls HA, persists policy, builds a prompt, or serializes a listener payload. An allowlist covers weather, climate, vacuum, sun, and curated coffee; weather/climate temperatures collapse into one `ambient.temperature` topic. A fact is reserved only after queue admission and starts its cooldown only at stream start, so a discarded segment never claims it was heard.
#822:- **Entity policy v1 to v2** (`home/entity_policy.py`) — adds `personal_moment_opt_ins` and a monotonic `policy_revision`. Migration keeps v1 mutes; malformed or unknown-schema files never grant a personal-moment permission (fail-closed).
#822:- **`PATCH /api/homeassistant/entity-policy`** — now applies exactly one of `muted` or `personal_moment_enabled`; a room-presence opt-in is gated on a live-eligibility check, and tightening privacy (mute, or revoking consent) pulls any unstarted queued break for that entity while the airing segment finishes untouched.
#822:- **Producer + scriptwriter** — one fact per casual break, reserved at admission and discarded if its policy went stale before air; `write_banter` enforces a `home_fact_id` contract with a single bounded repair, falling back to fact-free banter rather than dropping good copy.
#822:- **Privacy** — `home_fact_*` metadata is scrubbed recursively from `/public-status`, queue projections, now-playing, and stream logs; `/status` receives only count-based diagnostics. Admin gains the personal-moment toggle and a fact-free rotation-state row.
#822:
#822:### Pre-ship review squad (3 agents) — findings resolved
#822:- **Adversarial, high severity:** `activate()` returned before popping the reservation/topic lock on a stale-revision or fact-id mismatch. Since `activate()` runs once at stream start and an aired segment never hits `release()`, any unrelated entity-policy toggle (which bumps the global `policy_revision` on the next HA poll) permanently leaked the `ambient.temperature` topic family for the session. Fixed: pop first, then evaluate, mirroring `release()`. Regression test added [proof: tests].
#822:- **Adversarial, medium severity:** the entity-policy endpoint dropped `invalidate_entity`'s returned pending queue ids, so a fact reserved at admission but still mid-egress render was not released. Fixed: the endpoint now releases those ids explicitly. Regression test added [proof: tests].
#822:- **Coverage:** added the director-exception audio-safety guard tests, the personal-moment eligibility 422 gate, and the exactly-one-action PATCH contract [proof: tests].
#822:- **Docs:** fixed a stale `docs/operations.md` endpoint summary still describing the old single-`muted` contract.
#822:

#823:## What this does
#823:
#823:A mobile-first QA pass that makes the listener page and the admin producer desk tell the truth about their own state, plus the CI scaffolding to keep both honest.
#823:
#823:**Listener (player):**
#823:- Every play surface switches visibly and accessibly between Listen and Pause; a stopped station shows an honest paused status instead of a false Resume; dedication fields never start audio. [proof: honesty]
#823:- Empty dedications explain what is missing, successful requests stay visible, failed requests preserve the listener's message, and all outcomes route through warm human copy (no "429"/"timeout"/"rejected" on screen). [proof: honesty]
#823:- Stale browser data can no longer replace the station name served by the radio.
#823:- A subtle "Live from your home" strip surfaces the recent home moments the hosts actually reacted to, as plain labels only.
#823:
#823:**Admin (producer desk):**
#823:- The live console fits 320px with full-size controls; backstage work is labelled as building ahead, not live; a failed status poll shows a reconnecting state instead of a frozen desk.
#823:- A stopped session rejects Skip, Air Next, Next-track, and Panic Cut with warm way-out copy until the operator presses Start. [proof: tests]
#823:- Skip commits every transport mutation before its first yield, so a concurrent Stop stays the final state; skip-history persistence failures can no longer turn a successful cut into an operator-facing error. [proof: tests]
#823:- First paint is seeded with the real stopped state via a `data-stopped` body attribute so the desk is truthful before the first status poll returns.
#823:- Production render is isolated so a malformed production shape can never starve the stopped-state honesty updaters (would otherwise show live controls over a paused station). [proof: tests]
#823:
#823:**Docs + CI:**
#823:- Install and recovery guidance aligned per package (Home Assistant Apps path, Docker quickstart, source checkout, Edge channel); recovery now routes through branch to CI image to planned update instead of live file edits.
#823:- New docs-safety lint blocks live-surgery recovery steps from re-entering the docs; new player and admin browser smokes assert real interaction outcomes against a live server in CI (no continue-on-error). [proof: tests]
#823:
#823:No version bump — this rides the dev-first soak model and a public tag is a separate explicit step.
#823:

#829:## What changed
#829:
#829:Program-replacing operator controls now protect on-air continuity as a single atomic step. Source switches, playlist purges, panic, Chaos and Festival cutovers, and the everyday shuffle / add / move / ban / dismiss playlist edits rebuild the real playback queue **and** its Scaletta shadow together, and reserve only audio that is already safe to play right now: the packaged continuity clip first, then eligible normalized-cache music that passes the same blocklist gate as any other admission, then a new packaged `emergency_tone.mp3` as the cold-cache last resort. A `continuity_epoch` counter is bumped on every rebuild; producer and startup-prewarm work captures the epoch and discards its render if the epoch changed before admission (including after egress), so a render begun for the old lineup can never arrive after the control action. A just-banned or just-removed song cannot re-enter through this instant-audio reserve. [proof: tests]
#829:
#829:Also adds bounded, admin-only `render_timings` diagnostics on `/status` (newest-first, retained ≤20, `produced`/`discarded`/`failed` with per-stage durations) and an admin-only `continuity_slot` projection of any reserved capacity-exempt safety audio. Both are diagnostics only — absent from `/public-status`, never scheduling input, never able to affect what airs. The admin Engine Room renders them as two new "Last render" and "Protected continuity" rows.
#829:
#829:New capacity-exempt `continuity_slot` on `StationState` holds a safety reservation that playback consumes only after the real queue drains, so a full queue can never block a safety reservation.
#829:
#829:## Why
#829:
#829:A control that rebuilt the queue could open a gap, admit a render built for the old lineup, or let a just-banned/removed song re-enter through the norm-cache instant-audio path. This makes every program-replacing control honor one reservation contract, keeps the shadow rundown in lockstep with the real queue, and guarantees silence is never the terminal state.
#829:
#829:## QA Impact
#829:
#829:Classification: Both — deferred to release candidate
#829:Reason:
#829:- Touched surfaces: listener audio path (continuity reservation, fallback ladder) and admin Engine Room (two additive read-only diagnostic rows).
#829:- Why this QA scope is sufficient: this merges into the `[Unreleased]` trunk with no version bump — nothing reaches the Pi until a release candidate is cut and landed. Automated coverage is comprehensive: the full suite (4611 passed), the three mandatory audio-delivery scenarios (normal / empty-fallback / post-restart) verified present by the coverage audit, plus new tests pinning the exclusion contract and the live index population. The admin changes are additive diagnostic rows using existing status states (blue/amber/gray, no green), no protected UI element touched.
#829:
#829:QA performed:
#829:- Player QA: deferred to release candidate
#829:- Admin QA: deferred to release candidate
#829:
#829:## Known follow-ups (from pre-merge review, to land on this branch before release)
#829:
#829:- The reservation scan reads norm-cache sidecars synchronously on the event loop across the control endpoints. Worst case (many dead/blocklisted cache entries while the runway is already thin) this can stall the loop for a few hundred ms on slow Pi storage. No dead air (the rescue ladder still covers it) and no crash, but it is an instant-audio latency risk worth moving off the loop (or carrying artist/title in the index so no sidecar read is needed on the control path).
#829:- `immediate_audio_index` is not size-bounded; cap it to live cache membership and prune on eviction.
#829:- Add a last-mile in-memory blocklist check at capacity-exempt slot consumption (only reachable via a corrupt sidecar, but the gate-less slot path deserves the same guard as the queue path).
#829:- A slot-only reservation bumps `continuity_epoch` even when the real queue does not change; scope the bump to real queue mutations to avoid discarding in-flight renders under rapid operator input.
#829:

#833:## What & why
#833:
#833:The listener page hardcoded **"320 kbps"** in four places (the "Codice" about-card and the three ticker repetitions), but the stream encodes at the configured bitrate — `radio.toml` sets `bitrate = 192`. The UI was telling listeners the stream was 320 kbps when it never delivers that. This renders the canonical `stream_audio_metadata(config)["bitrate_kbps"]` instead, so the visible number always matches `/public-status`, the `/stream` ICY headers, and the actual encode.
#833:
#833:- `_listener_context()` (`mammamiradio/web/streamer.py`) now exposes `stream_bitrate_kbps` from the same helper already used by the `/public-status` and `/stream` sites.
#833:- `listener.html` renders `{{ stream_bitrate_kbps }} kbps` at all four sites.
#833:- Route tests assert each visible site class independently: the ungated about-card, the three frequency-gated ticker repetitions, and a blank-frequency case where only the about-card survives — all against config (192/128), with no stale `320 kbps`.
#833:- `uv.lock` synced `2.17.0 → 2.18.0` to reconcile drift left by the #830 release (pyproject + config.yaml are already 2.18.0 on `main`). Not a version bump.

#849:## What changed
#849:
#849:A temporary Anthropic overload or rate limit (HTTP 429 or 529) now briefly benches the AI writer and sends affected later host breaks straight to the OpenAI backup writer, then returns to Anthropic automatically once a short cooldown clears. Before this, a transient pressure spike made listeners wait through the same failing request again before any fallback kicked in. [proof: tests]
#849:
#849:- A 429 rate limit is scoped to the failing model; a 529 overload benches Anthropic account-wide. Both cooldowns are short and self-healing. [proof: tests]
#849:- The cooldown honors a `Retry-After` header when the provider sends one, clamped to a sane 5–60 second window (default 20s), and ignores garbage, negative, or non-finite values. [proof: tests]
#849:- A `billing_error` is now classified by the SDK error type as an account-wide usage block rather than slipping through fuzzy text matching. [proof: tests]
#849:- The provider's own SDK retries are disabled on this call so the station's circuit breaker is the single retry authority — no hidden retry storm behind the breaker. [proof: tests]
#849:- If no OpenAI key is configured, a transient error falls through to deterministic stock copy without benching Anthropic, so the very next segment can still reach the primary writer. Silence is never the outcome. [proof: tests]
#849:
#849:## Operator-facing surface
#849:
#849:The admin Engine Room provider-status line now reads "Temporarily unavailable; OpenAI fallback" (instead of the auth-specific wording) when Anthropic is benched, since the same status now covers transient causes, and the retry countdown shows seconds under a minute instead of rounding everything up to "1 min". The transient state reports as self-recovering, so an operator sees "no action needed" rather than a false action-required alarm.
#849:
#849:## Docs
#849:
#849:- `docs/architecture.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` (Unreleased) describe the new fallback behavior.
#849:- `docs/troubleshooting.md` now lists the two new `anthropic_transient` / `anthropic_transient_blocked` fallback reasons and documents the short overload breaker alongside the existing 10-minute auth/config breaker.
#849:
#849:## QA Impact
#849:Classification: Admin
#849:Reason:
#849:- Touched surfaces: admin Engine Room provider-status copy and countdown (`updateEngineRoom`, `runtimeProviderRow`); the rest of the change is the backend scriptwriter fallback path, which has no listener-facing surface.
#849:- Why this QA scope is sufficient: the only UI change is provider-status copy strings, pinned by static invariant tests in `tests/web/test_admin_status_invariants.py`. The transient state itself only manifests under a live Anthropic 429/529, which is not reproducible in a manual QA session; the unit tests exercise every branch.
#849:QA performed:
#849:- Player QA: not applicable — no listener-facing surface changed
#849:- Admin QA: deferred to release candidate — copy is statically test-pinned; full Admin QA runs on the final candidate before public release

#849:
#850:## What & why
#850:
#850:The admin Engine Room's estimated AI spend was billed *after* a cloud voice finished local post-processing. A paid voice (OpenAI / Azure / ElevenLabs) that the provider had already charged for, but which then hit a snag during loudnorm or the raw-file write, fell through to Edge and was counted as free — real money, zero on the meter. This bills the session estimate the moment the provider confirms its response, with an idempotency guard so a success callback can never double-count. OpenAI schedules that callback thread-safe from its executor worker, so a request that completes after the local timeout still counts.
#850:
#850:The Engine Room now shows a "Session estimate" line whenever there is real paid usage, including voice-only sessions with no other AI calls — previously the estimate only appeared once there were AI calls, so a TTS-only session showed nothing.
#850:
#850:The accounting path is best-effort throughout and can never raise into audio; a voice with missing credentials or a failure before the provider responds stays uncounted. [proof: tests]
#850:
#850:## Changes
#850:
#850:- `mammamiradio/audio/tts.py` — an `on_paid_provider_success` callback is threaded into the three cloud synths and fires on the confirmed paid response; a `billed` nonlocal guard makes it count once; OpenAI schedules it via `loop.call_soon_threadsafe`.
#850:- `mammamiradio/web/templates/admin.html` — the "Session estimate" line is gated on real paid usage; the protected `apiCostEl` counter and the cost split are preserved.
#850:- Tests — bill-once per provider, no double-count when post-processing falls back to Edge, zero-bill before the paid response, the loop-closed skip, and a new guard test for the double-callback case; admin browser smoke and regia-polish cover the estimate line.
#850:- `docs/architecture.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` updated to match.
#850:

#850:
#851:## What changed
#851:
#851:Fresh installations now start with a deliberately small Home Assistant context instead of inheriting a household's full home state by default. A new install-scoped authorization layer (`home/authorization.py`) projects a cold install down to synthetic coarse daylight (`sun.ambient`) plus, only when exactly one unambiguous `weather.*` source exists, one coarse banded weather reading (`weather.ambient`); every other entity, generated label, mood, reactive moment, timer, running gag, and saved moment-trail projection is withheld. Existing stations keep their current home behavior through a fail-closed continuity bridge (`home/migration.py`) keyed on paired durable-sidecar and database-local install-origin witnesses — missing, corrupt, disagreeing, or transplanted witnesses all fail narrow, so an update never silences a house that already chose full context and a leftover witness can never promote a cold install. [proof: tests]
#851:
#851:Authorization mode travels with every home-context snapshot: fresh, stale, timeout, and module-cache paths all reject a context stamped for the other mode, so the two modes never cross. [proof: tests] The producer's single-flight home-context coordinator threads the active mode through its fetch and discards any adopted result stamped for the wrong mode. A new `scheduling/queue_mutations.py` boundary (`drop_matching_segments`) centralizes queued-segment removal so a banned or removed song is purged consistently from the real queue and its shadow rundown in one step. [proof: tests]
#851:
#851:Narrow installs also skip registry/name loading and the weather-forecast arc, and do not project persisted moment receipts onto `/public-status` or `/status`; the manual label-regeneration route reports no candidates. [proof: tests]
#851:
#851:## Why
#851:
#851:Any Home-Assistant-enabled install used to receive the full home projection the moment a token was present. Authorization should be earned from an install's own provenance, not assumed on first boot — a fresh install must fail closed to coarse ambient basics, and only a genuine pre-existing install keeps the established household feature set. Every home path stays best-effort: an authorization or witness failure degrades context, it never stalls or dead-airs the audio path.
#851:

#867:## What changed
#867:
#867:Marco and Giulia can now use a more expressive ElevenLabs V3 delivery without changing what the station says. A small, character-specific set of performance cues (Marco: energetic, curious, playful; Giulia: dry, curious, playful) is applied only at the final voice request. The clean spoken line stays the sole input to transcripts, safety and language guards, memory, paid-TTS accounting, and Edge fallback, so a failed V3 request can never make a fallback voice read markup aloud. [proof: tests]
#867:
#867:Non-banter host speech (transitions, news flashes, ad intros) now renders under the same host's V3 model, and any model-emitted bracket direction is stripped at the provider boundary. Only the code-owned cue can ever reach V3 as an audio tag, so an LLM cannot smuggle uncontrolled performance markup into a live segment. [proof: tests]
#867:
#867:Host voice changes now ship with a real V2-versus-V3 listening gate. The audition tool renders matched clean and expressive samples for both regular hosts, then saves an immutable, redacted proof receipt with hashes, provider outcome, audio evidence, and a human decision. It never stores raw copy, audio paths, or credentials. `--verify-host-performance-gate` blocks an edge release unless every paired Marco and Giulia row was generated and accepted. [proof: tests]
#867:
#867:New `radio.toml` `[[hosts]]` keys: `elevenlabs_model` (default `eleven_multilingual_v2`) and `delivery_profile` (default `none`). V2 hosts, ads, sweepers, and every other voice are unchanged.

#873:## What changed
#873:
#873:When live production stalls and the station bridges on already-normalized ("norm-cache") music, selection was a random pick — so the *same* cached song could air three times in about twenty minutes. That is an obvious "this is a machine" tell and breaks the radio illusion.
#873:
#873:This adds a session-scoped **rescue-rotation cooldown**:
#873:
#873:- A cached song that actually airs as a rescue rests for one hour of real time before it can be picked again.
#873:- While it rests, rotation prefers a fresher cached track.
#873:- When every cached track is still resting, the station airs the one heard longest ago (round-robin) — so a listener gets a real song they last heard twenty minutes ago instead of the same one a third time.
#873:- Music always plays: the guard never introduces silence or drops to a tone when a cached song is available.
#873:- The cooldown is fed only when a rescue is truly heard by a listener (bytes reached the room, not skipped) and resets on restart.
#873:- The control room gains an admin-only "Cached rotation" readout so an operator can see it working. The listener payload is unchanged.
#873:
#873:Both the producer/live-control continuity reserve and the playback-gap fill share the one cooldown.
#873:

The rescue path fires only during producer stalls and produces the same kind of cached-music audio it already produced; `rescue_rotation` is proven absent from `/public-status`. #878:## Summary
#878:
#878:Follow-up to #872 (66719a6f, fail-closed TTS). Cancelling a TTS/ad/dialogue render no longer races executor-backed FFmpeg work: `_settle_owned`/`_settle_executor` (`mammamiradio/audio/tts.py`) and `_gather_all_settled`/`_raise_first_settled_error` (`mammamiradio/scheduling/producer.py`) now shield owned concurrent fan-outs with `asyncio.shield`, re-awaiting on repeated cancellation, so scratch-file cleanup only runs after every sibling (including executor-backed FFmpeg work) has actually settled. This closes the exact "executor-cancellation-cleanup" race a prior review flagged as CRITICAL on the original commit.

#882:## Summary
#882:
#882:Continues the playable-runway safety work from #871/#874 — closes the remaining ways the producer/streamer could count queued or reserved audio as "ready" when it could never actually reach air.
#882:
#882:**Runway accounting**
#882:- Every runway/headroom computation (`_reserve_continuity_runway`, `_producer_headroom_snapshot`, `_playable_runway_available`, `/api/skip`, `/api/panic`, `/public-status`) now only counts a segment's duration toward available runway when it is immediately playable — not blocklisted, not a stale companionship cue, and present as a non-empty regular file on disk.
#882:- A last-mile fence in `run_playback_loop` discards a banned track that was already pulled off the queue, before any bytes reach air, and reconciles tail-adjacency bookkeeping afterward.
#882:- `_discard_unplayable_queue_prefix` strips a dead queue prefix so `/api/skip` bridges to fresh music only when there's genuinely no playable runway left, not just an empty-looking queue.
#882:- `_blocklist_safe_last_music` centralizes the banned/unidentified-last-known-good-music fence shared by error recovery, the quality-gate circuit breaker, and speech-bed adjacency.
#882:
#882:**Found during this ship's review** (adversarial + specialist review, see below):
#882:- `_apply_ban`'s new fail-closed tail-adjacency guard (`_reconcile_queue_tail_adjacency`) had a sibling gap: `queue_remove_item` (`POST /api/queue/remove`, manual single-item removal from the admin UI) has the identical arbitrary-removal shape but was still using `_rebuild_queue_shadow`'s naive re-anchor. An operator manually removing the queue tail could silently reintroduce an untrusted, possibly egress-processed segment as a "clean" speech-bed source. Fixed and covered by a regression test that fails without the fix.
#882:- A `assert last_good_payload is not None` in the quality-gate circuit breaker was pure type-narrowing that becomes a no-op under `python -O`; replaced with a plain `if`/`else`.
#882:- A missing regression test for `_reconcile_queue_tail_adjacency`'s fail-closed branch (ordinary, non-rescue music exposed as the new tail must not reanchor) — added, verified it fails without the underlying guard.

#884:## What & why
#884:
#884:Admin control-room rotation edits (Ban, ▶ Next, drag-to-reorder, search "Next") trusted a bare row **index**. When the playlist shifted underneath the operator — a source switch, the 3s status poll, or a concurrent edit — that index could point at a different song by the time the click landed, so a **Ban or Next could hit the wrong track** [proof: tests].
#884:
#884:Every rotation-row mutation now uses optimistic concurrency: the client echoes `{revision, index, id}` from the exact rendered snapshot, and the server revalidates under `source_switch_lock` before mutating:
#884:
#884:- `422 invalid_target` — missing/malformed fields (never mutates)
#884:- `409 stale_playlist` — revision, index, or opaque row token no longer matches (the UI shows "the rotation changed, refresh and try again")
#884:- `409 rotation_updating` — a source/rotation update owns the lock right now (recoverable by retry)
#884:
#884:Search results and the operator preference control now key on song **identity**, not position, so a stale search result can't redirect a click. Serialized admin tracks carry an opaque row `id` (`spotify_id` → `cache_key`); duplicate tokens stay disambiguated by index. Successful edits return the new `playlist_revision`.
#884:
#884:Affected routes: `/api/playlist/remove`, `/api/playlist/move`, `/api/playlist/move_to_next`, `/api/search`, `/api/playlist`. Docs updated in `docs/architecture.md` (route contract table + conflict-status paragraph + source-switch concurrency).
#884:
#884:No change to the audio path — these are admin routes; `_reserve_continuity_runway` and `_apply_ban` run synchronously inside the lock with no await-while-held, so there's no dead-air risk [proof: tests].
#884:

#884:

#884:Reason:
#884:- Touched surfaces: control-room rotation controls (Ban / Next / drag-reorder / search), admin routes `/api/playlist/*` and `/api/search`, `admin.html` client. No listener-facing surface: `/public-status`, listener UI, and the audio pipeline are unchanged; `_serialize_track`'s new `id` is only consumed by admin playlist/search.
#884:- Why this QA scope is sufficient: the change is entirely operator-facing. Client contract paths (stale-search invalidation, crossed-page revision, 409 recovery toast, post-restart lower-revision adoption, drag revision-mismatch) are covered by `tests/web/admin_browser_smoke.js`; server paths by the full route matrix in `tests/web/test_streamer_routes_extended.py`.

#884:
#886:## What
#886:
#886:When a cloud voice provider (OpenAI, Azure, ElevenLabs) fails, the station now records why and degrades honestly instead of silently:
#886:
#886:- Every runtime cloud-to-Edge fallback emits a route record (`TTS fallback provider=... reason=...`) and a distinct `Synthesized (Edge fallback)` log line, so intentional Edge casting and silent premium-provider failure are distinguishable [proof: tests].
#886:- Each provider route carries a circuit breaker: a route-wide failure (timeout, 5xx, revoked key) sends waiting and later parts straight to Edge, transient failures cool down 30 seconds and then exactly one call probes the provider, and auth failures stay disabled for the session [proof: tests].
#886:- A single bad voice ID (HTTP 400/404) sidelines only that voice — every other character on the same provider keeps its cloud voice, on all three engines including the OpenAI SDK's own error types [proof: tests].
#886:- Healthy voices sharing one provider route render concurrently, and a call queued behind an outage re-checks the breaker after taking its render slot so a multi-voice ad cannot stack timeout waves [proof: tests].
#886:- The admin runtime card and `/api/capabilities` reflect live degradation, with every internal reason token translated to plain operator copy per engine (raw values remain as `diagnostic_reason` for authenticated API consumers) [proof: tests].
#886:
#886:## Why
#886:
#886:A provider-wide outage used to cost a full cloud timeout for every ad part, and a live cloud fallback was indistinguishable from intentional Edge casting in both logs and the admin panel. Dialogue lines on a shared provider must also keep rendering in parallel — slower breaks mean a shallower production runway.
#886:
