#989:The recipe-driven ad prompt asks the writer for voice and pause parts only. The post-parse filter that claims to enforce that prompt dropped just `sfx`, so `environment` parts survived it — and because `AdPart.type` is copied straight from model JSON with no validation, so did every other token a model can invent.
#989:
#989:This replaces the denylist with the allowlist the prompt already states.
#989:
#989:```python
#989:- return [part for part in parts if part.type != "sfx"]
#989:+ return [part for part in parts if part.type in ("voice", "pause")]
#989:```
#989:
#989:## Not an audio change
#989:
#989:Worth stating plainly, because the shape of the diff suggests otherwise: no listener hears a difference [proof: tests].
#989:
#989:An `environment` part never reached audio on any path. `synthesize_ad` builds its render list from `("voice", "sfx", "pause")` at `mammamiradio/audio/tts.py:1450`, and `_render_part` has no branch for the type. Ad ambience comes from `script.sonic.environment`, a different object on `SonicWorld`, read at `tts.py:1824` and never from the parts list — so the foley layer is unaffected regardless of which bed path runs, including the fallback where a recipe with a missing bed or cue asset drops through to the legacy bed tasks.
#989:
#989:So this is a contract fix, not a sound fix. The value is that the boundary now enforces what it says it enforces, and cannot silently pass the next invented type.
#989:
#989:## Why an allowlist
#989:
#989:`sfx` was caught first. `environment` had to be added behind it. A denylist only ever catches the tokens someone already thought of, and there is no validation upstream to fall back on:
#989:
#989:```python
#989:type=p.get("type", "voice"),   # scriptwriter.py:3747
#989:```
#989:
#989:The new test feeds `ambience` and `music` part types and asserts only voice and pause survive. It fails against the previous denylist and passes against the allowlist [proof: tests] — so a third instance of this gets caught by CI rather than by a reader.
#989:
#989:`AdPart.type` has exactly four documented values, so the inversion is behavior-identical today.
#989:
#989:Also in the diff: the function docstring no longer claims a dropped environment part would "recreate the very layered drone", which the render boundary already prevented; and the legacy-path assertion now snapshots its input with `deepcopy` before comparing, because the branch shallow-copies the list and writes fields in place, so comparing against the same list object read as equal even through a real mutation.
#989:
#989:No CHANGELOG entry: nothing here is audible or operator-visible, so an entry would describe a non-change. Doc sync is covered by `docs/architecture.md`.
#989:
#989:Follow-ups filed rather than bundled: #985 (ad pause duration reaches ffmpeg unclamped), #986 (`AdPart.environment` is written and never read), #987 (the recipe prompt names an environment it then forbids).
#989:

#990:A specification for moving admitted-audio queue ownership behind one internal module, preserving current listener, operator, HTTP, and Home Assistant behaviour. It covers ownership boundaries, queue invariants, a 21-commit plan across three correctness slices and four architecture cuts, the focused test suite, Edge proof requirements, and backout.
#990:
#990:This is the specification only. No runtime code changes here, and no cut is authorised by merging it.
#990:
#990:### Reconciled against current `main`, not the July snapshot
#990:
#990:The original review was taken at `776d8cf7` in late July. Rather than land a plan describing code that has since moved, the document now records what `7e6deecd` already changed, and corrects itself:
#990:
#990:- `scheduling/queue_mutations.py` already owns drop/rebuild and calls `segment.release()`, so the plan absorbs it instead of re-extracting a second drain/filter/rebuild.
#990:- Restart handoff already refuses Jamendo, starter, unknown, and add-on-external sources, so routing it through the owner must preserve those filters rather than the July "any safe music" wording.
#990:- Stop invalidation already advances `continuity_epoch` before cleanup, so the plan reuses that fence and explicitly forbids inventing a second generation counter. The remaining work is proof, not coverage.
#990:
#990:Two changes are worth calling out because they protect things that are easy to break.
#990:
#990:**The ownership scanner moves to the front, report-only.** It was the last commit; it is now the first, so it measures every cut instead of first running against twelve merged ones. The plan also records that a loose match would flag `mammamiradio/integrations/now_playing.py:98` — a local read-only assignment inside the **frozen** v1 contract surface. That file cannot be edited to satisfy a guard, so a false positive there is a hard block rather than a nit, and the scan excludes `mammamiradio/integrations/**` explicitly.
#990:
#990:**Three rescue paths stay deliberately unfenced.** The two quality-gate circuit-breaker inserts and the playback gap fill omit the staleness check on purpose. They are the last audio between a listener and silence, so the plan records them as intentional and puts them out of scope rather than treating them as an open question.
#990:
#990:Backout is now explicit: a cut is revertible as one PR until the sealing cut removes the compatibility re-exports, after which it is corrected forward. Recovery on the Edge Pi is an add-on version pin to the previous tag — never a container change or a process signal.
#990:
#990:The test baseline was re-pinned: 311 passing at the July snapshot against a shorter list, 1560 against the current list, with four files added because they actually exercise the code being moved.

#991:Grouped Dependabot titles carry `in the <group> group across 1 directory` and pass the 72-character subject limit by construction, so every grouped dependency PR failed `commit-lint` and needed a manual retitle. Seven were stuck behind it at once.
#991:
#991:Two defects upstream caused it, both now fixed in `engineering-standards`:
#991:
#991:- The reusable workflow hardcoded a check for a lone `WHY_REQUIRED`, which made `exemptions.trusted_bot_skips` decorative — editing that array changed nothing. CI now resolves it from the vendored rules.
#991:- The PR-title check consulted no bot allowlist at all; only the commit loop did. Since the title becomes the squash-merge subject, every grouped bot PR failed there regardless of author.
#991:
#991:This re-pins the workflow to `b7f5ba76136c577f511edaa0f59d50b06bfd3c1a` and vendors rules schema 1.2.0, where `SUBJECT_TOO_LONG` joins the skip list. A bot tripping any rule outside that list still fails, so this is not a general bypass.
#991:
#991:The rules file is copied verbatim from upstream at that commit and verified byte-identical rather than hand-edited, per the standing rule against hand-editing the vendored copy. The only differences from the previous vendored copy are the schema bump and the new skip entry.
#991:
#991:`CONTRIBUTING.md`'s bot-allowlist section said bots skip `WHY_REQUIRED`, which is no longer accurate; it now points at `trusted_bot_skips` and states that one non-skippable violation still fails.

#993:The nudge that exists to break the strict-status-checks deadlock was silently no-opping through it.
#993:
#993:Run [32342094107](https://github.com/florianhorner/mammamiradio/actions/runs/32342094107) logged `nudge: no behind Dependabot PRs — nothing to do` two seconds after a push to main, while four were behind and two had been parked since 17 August. GitHub computes `mergeStateStatus` lazily, so immediately after a push to the base branch it answers `UNKNOWN` for every open PR — and this workflow runs `on: push` to main, asking in exactly that window. A `BEHIND` filter against an `UNKNOWN` answer matches nothing and reads as "fine".
#993:
#993:## What changed
#993:
#993:It now re-asks while any PR still reports `UNKNOWN`, bounded by `NUDGE_MERGE_STATE_TRIES` (6) and `NUDGE_MERGE_STATE_DELAY` (10s). A still-`UNKNOWN` reply is left alone rather than guessed as `BEHIND` [proof: tests].
#993:
#993:Each attempt is a single `gh pr list` call serving both audiences, partitioned on `.author.login`. Querying per-author would pay the `UNKNOWN` wait twice and let a Dependabot PR land in both the nudge set and the human-escalation set — nudged and escalated at once [proof: tests]. It also passes an explicit `--limit 100`; the CLI default of 30 would silently truncate, which is the same bug one level down.
#993:
#993:Human-authored PRs deadlock the same way but cannot be fixed from CI: a `GITHUB_TOKEN` `update-branch` moves the head without retriggering checks, leaving the PR waiting on results that never arrive. Armed ones are named in a workflow warning and step summary pointing at `scripts/land-pr.sh`, which updates the branch after verifying pre-ship evidence, rather than a bare `update-branch` that would route around the landing contract.
#993:
#993:Both retry budgets and the list limit fall back to their defaults on non-numeric input: a bare arithmetic for-loop would silently never run, turning a typo into a dead mechanism [proof: tests].
#993:
#993:## Why the tests grew from 9 to 26
#993:
#993:The list mock now returns raw JSON, so the script's own filtering is exercised rather than mocked away. The previous hostile-input case turned out to be inert — it passed with every identifier guard deleted, because it asserted only that no comment was posted and the mock had no view fixture for the junk key.
#993:
#993:Two mutations that survived the old suite now fail it: removing every PR-identifier guard, and removing the step-summary appendability probe [proof: tests].
#993:
